title: Congo's Deadliest Ebola Outbreak Passes 10,000 Cases
title_zh: 刚果史上最严重埃博拉疫情确诊超一万例
source_name: UN News — “DR Congo: WHO urges sustained efforts as Ebola cases top 10,000” (28 Oct 2026)
summary_zh: 刚果民主共和国由布尼亚病毒引起的埃博拉疫情已是该国史上最大、全球第二大；截至十月底病例逾一万、死亡近五千至五千以上。世卫组织呼吁扩大防控、深入难进地区并建立社区信任；环状接种试验与候选疫苗评估正在进行，肯尼亚等国已出现输入病例。本文适合积累公共卫生、疫情防控与国际合作类雅思词汇。
paragraphs: Health officials in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) report that the country's current Ebola outbreak has grown into its largest on record. By late October 2026, confirmed cases had climbed past 10,000, and deaths were approaching or just above 5,000. The World Health Organization (WHO) says this is also the second-largest Ebola outbreak in the world, after the West Africa epidemic of 2014–2016.

The disease is caused by the rare Bundibugyo virus. Unlike the better-known Zaire strain, there is still no licensed vaccine or specific treatment for Bundibugyo. The outbreak was declared in mid-May and began in the east of the country, where conflict, hunger and displacement make medical work especially hard. It has now reached eight provinces, including areas that responders struggle to enter.

WHO stresses that "sustained efforts" are essential. That means scaling up control measures, gaining greater access to affected communities, and building trust so that people seek care early. Roughly half of those infected have died, and many deaths still happen in the community before patients reach a treatment centre — a sign that detection and access remain weak.

There are also signs of progress. More than 2,600 people have recovered. Testing and treatment capacity have expanded, and clinical trials of candidate vaccines are under way. The TUMAINI trials — "hope" in Swahili — first check whether the Ervebo vaccine, made for the Zaire strain, can protect contacts of confirmed patients through a ring-vaccination approach. Experts are also reviewing vaccines designed specifically against Bundibugyo.

Cross-border risk is real. Kenya has recorded a small cluster of cases linked to a traveller from the DRC, and Nigeria confirmed an imported case. A UN humanitarian fund has sent more than two million dollars to strengthen Kenya's border checks, training and preparedness. WHO advises against travel or trade bans, but urges neighbouring countries to stay ready.

For IELTS learners, this story connects public health, inequality and international cooperation. Notice how the text balances hard numbers with causes (conflict, limited access) and responses (surveillance, trials, community outreach). Similar cause–effect and problem–solution patterns often appear in Reading and in Writing Task 2 essays on disease and development.
paragraphs_zh: 刚果民主共和国（DRC）卫生官员报告称，该国当前的埃博拉疫情已发展成有记录以来规模最大的一次。到2026年10月下旬，确诊病例已超过一万，死亡人数接近或刚刚超过五千。世界卫生组织（WHO）表示，这也是全球第二大埃博拉疫情，仅次于2014至2016年的西非疫情。
此次疾病由罕见的布尼亚病毒引起。与更广为人知的扎伊尔毒株不同，目前仍没有针对布尼亚病毒的获批疫苗或特效治疗。疫情于5月中旬宣布，始于该国东部；那里冲突、饥饿与流离失所使医疗工作格外艰难。疫情现已波及八个省，其中包括救援人员难以进入的地区。
世卫组织强调，「持续努力」至关重要。这意味着要扩大防控措施、更多地进入受影响社区，并建立信任，好让人们尽早求医。感染者中约有一半死亡，而且许多死亡仍发生在社区、患者尚未抵达治疗中心之前——这说明发现病例与获得救治的能力仍然薄弱。
也有进展的迹象。已有逾两千六百人康复。检测与治疗能力有所扩大，候选疫苗的临床试验正在进行。名为 TUMAINI（斯瓦希里语「希望」）的试验首先检验：为扎伊尔毒株研制的 Ervebo 疫苗，能否通过环状接种保护确诊患者的密切接触者。专家们也在评估专门针对布尼亚病毒的疫苗。
跨境风险是真实存在的。肯尼亚已记录到与一名从刚果民主共和国入境旅客相关的一小群病例，尼日利亚也确认了一例输入病例。联合国人道主义基金已拨款逾两百万美元，加强肯尼亚的边境检查、培训与应急准备。世卫组织不主张实施旅行或贸易禁令，但敦促邻国保持戒备。
对雅思学习者来说，这篇报道把公共卫生、不平等与国际合作联系在一起。注意文章如何在硬数字之外，写出原因（冲突、准入受限）与应对（监测、试验、社区外展）。类似的「因果」和「问题—解决」展开方式，常出现在阅读以及疾病与发展类写作任务二中。
